Action Plan:
1. Acute left-sided throbbing headache with aura managed as probable migraine: advise trial of simple analgesia (Paracetamol) ± compound analgesia (Co-codamol) and NSAIDs (Ibuprofen or Naproxen; doses/route/frequency not documented).  
2. Initiate headache diary to identify frequency and potential triggers.  
3. Safety-net: return immediately if headache worsens, fails to improve within 2–3 days, or if red-flag symptoms develop (focal neurologic deficit, visual loss, persisting vomiting, neck stiffness).  
4. Discuss possible migraine prophylaxis if attacks become more frequent/persistent; review at follow-up next week.  
5. Consider future review of combined oral contraceptive (Microgynon) use in context of migraine with aura.  
6. Provide reassurance regarding low likelihood of intracranial malignancy given current clinical picture.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• CC: “Terrible headache” since mid-day (few hours), left-sided, throbbing, worse with head/neck movement.  
• Aura: zig-zag lines and blurred vision in both eyes preceding pain. Photophobia present (wearing sunglasses).  
• Associated symptoms: nausea and two episodes of vomiting. No fever, rash, speech difficulty, limb weakness, balance problems, breathlessness, or recent head injury.  
• Previous similar episode a few weeks ago, lasted ~2 days, improved with rest and painkillers.  
Past Medical History: none reported.  
Medications: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive), dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Social History: Works in fashion industry; high job stress. Lives alone. Denies smoking and alcohol use. Limited exercise.  
Family History: Mother with migraines and underactive thyroid; no known brain tumors.  
Allergies: not discussed.

Objective:
• No in-person examination performed (telehealth consult).  
• No vitals measured.  
Investigations: none performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute headache with aura  
   – Assessment: Migraine with aura.  
   – Differential: tension-type headache, cluster headache, intracranial mass (patient concern), meningitis (less likely—no fever/neck stiffness).  
   – Investigations: none indicated at this stage.  
   – Treatment: Paracetamol, Co-codamol, Ibuprofen, or Naproxen (all dose/route/frequency not documented); rest; darkened environment.  
   – Referral: none currently; consider neurology referral if frequency/severity increases or atypical features develop.

2. Ongoing headache management & prophylaxis  
   – Assessment: Recurrent migraine.  
   – Investigations: headache diary to monitor triggers/frequency.  
   – Treatment: consider prophylactic migraine medication if ≥2–4 attacks/month or disabling—discussion planned at next visit.  
   – Referral: consider neurology if prophylaxis required or diagnostic uncertainty persists.

3. Combined oral contraceptive use with migraine aura  
   – Assessment: Potential increased vascular risk with estrogen-containing OCP in aura-positive migraine.  
   – Plan: Reassess suitability of Microgynon at follow-up; consider non-estrogen contraception if migraines persist or additional risk factors identified.

Quality checks:

● Missing but expected: confirmed drug allergies, vitals, basic neurological exam findings, dosage instructions for recommended medications, detailed contraceptive risk discussion.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear; occasional overlapping speech but clinically adequate.
